finding.summary: The New York Times reported from tax-return data that Trump’s federal income-tax liability was $750 in each of 2016 and 2017, and that he paid no income tax in 10 of the 15 years before his election. The $750 figure does not encompass all taxes: Trump or his companies also paid foreign taxes in 2017. A separately disclosed 2005 return showed $38 million in federal income tax. The Times did not have his personal returns for 2018 or 2019.

sources.title: Trump’s Taxes Show Chronic Losses and Years of Income Tax Avoidance
sources.snippet: Although he had more than enough credits to owe no taxes at all, his accountants appear to have carved out an allowance for a small tax liability for both 2016 and 2017. When they got to line 56, the one for income taxes due, the amount was the same each year: $750. ... The New York Times has obtained tax-return data extending over more than two decades for Mr. Trump and the hundreds of companies that make up his business organization, including detailed information from his first two years in office. It does not include his personal returns for 2018 or 2019.

finding.summary: In the September 26, 2016 presidential debate, Hillary Clinton said records from Trump’s casino-license applications showed that he had paid no federal income tax in certain years. Trump responded, “That makes me smart.” He did not say “Because I’m smart. I know how to game the system” in that exchange; those words are a paraphrase, not an exact quotation. At an October 3, 2016 rally, however, Trump separately said he had “brilliantly” used tax laws to his benefit.

report_raw.claim: Why should you pay more taxes than Donald Trump pays? And that’s a fact. $750. Remember what he said when that was raised a while ago, how he only pays … He said, ‘Because I’m smart. I know how to game the system.’
report_raw.justification: The New York Times reported that Trump’s federal income-tax liability was $750 in each of 2016 and 2017, based on tax-return data it obtained; those figures do not represent every kind of tax. [S1][S4] Modeling estimated that about half of U.S. tax units paid more than $750 in federal income tax in those years, but it cannot establish what an unspecified listener paid. [S5] In the 2016 debate exchange about paying no federal income tax, Trump said, “That makes me smart,” not the words presented here as a direct quotation. [S7][S8] He separately said he had “brilliantly” used tax laws to his benefit. [S9] Inference: The verdict turns on treating the attributed words as an exact quote and the 2016 debate as the exchange being recalled; the quotation misstates that exchange, although it conveys part of its substance.
key_points: The $750 figure is supported for federal income-tax liability in 2016 and 2017, not for all taxes or all years. [S1][S3][S4]
About half of modeled tax units paid more than $750 in federal income tax in those years; the listener’s payment is unknown. [S5]
The debate transcript records “That makes me smart,” rather than the quotation attributed to Trump in the claim. [S7][S8]
The transcript establishes what Trump said in that exchange, not whether he used the attributed words on another occasion. [S7]
report_raw.counter_argument: A case for Conflicting Evidence/Cherrypicking is that the $750 figure is supported and the attributed words paraphrase Trump’s actual remarks about being smart and using tax laws to his benefit. [S1][S7][S9] That verdict was not adopted because the claim presents specific words as a direct quotation, and the identified debate exchange does not contain them. [S7][S8]
evidence_gaps: The underlying 2016 and 2017 tax-return records used by The New York Times were not publicly released in the available evidence.
The available evidence does not establish the unspecified listener’s federal income-tax liability.
The debate transcript does not rule out Trump having used the attributed words on another occasion.
The Times reporting cited here did not include Trump’s personal returns for 2018 or 2019.

[S1][S7][S9] That verdict was not adopted because the claim presents specific words as a direct quotation, and the identified debate exchange does not contain them. [S7][S8]
evidence_gaps: The underlying 2016 and 2017 tax-return records used by The New York Times were not publicly released in the available evidence.
The available evidence does not establish the unspecified listener’s federal income-tax liability.
The debate transcript does not rule out Trump having used the attributed words on another occasion.
The Times reporting cited here did not include Trump’s personal returns for 2018 or 2019.

findings.question: For which tax year or years, if any, did Donald Trump pay $750 in federal income tax, and what do the available records show about his other tax payments?
findings.summary: The New York Times reported from tax-return data that Trump’s federal income-tax liability was $750 in each of 2016 and 2017, and that he paid no income tax in 10 of the 15 years before his election. The $750 figure does not encompass all taxes: Trump or his companies also paid foreign taxes in 2017. A separately disclosed 2005 return showed $38 million in federal income tax. The Times did not have his personal returns for 2018 or 2019.

findings.question: How did $750 in annual federal income tax compare with what U.S. taxpayers paid in the relevant year or years, and can the comparison be applied to an unspecified individual?
findings.summary: The New York Times reported that Trump’s federal income tax liability was $750 in each of 2016 and 2017. Tax Policy Center modeling estimated that about half of U.S. tax units paid more than $750 in federal income tax in those years. Separately, the Congressional Budget Office estimated that households in the middle income fifth paid an average of $2,200 in 2016. These comparisons do not establish what an unspecified listener paid.

findings.question: What did Donald Trump say in response to a claim that he paid little or no federal income tax, and did he say the quoted words “Because I’m smart. I know how to game the system”?
findings.summary: In the September 26, 2016 presidential debate, Hillary Clinton said records from Trump’s casino-license applications showed that he had paid no federal income tax in certain years. Trump responded, “That makes me smart.” He did not say “Because I’m smart. I know how to game the system” in that exchange; those words are a paraphrase, not an exact quotation. At an October 3, 2016 rally, however, Trump separately said he had “brilliantly” used tax laws to his benefit.

TRUMP: That makes me smart. CLINTON: So if he’s paid zero, that means zero for troops, zero for vets, zero for schools or health.
